nodes.description: RTL1 (PEG11, SIRH2) is a eutherian-specific paternally expressed gene derived from a Ty3/Gypsy (sushi-ichi-related) LTR retrotransposon. In KOS, RTL1 expression rises about five-fold with UPD(14)pat or epimutation and about 2.5-fold with deletions that spare one paternal-type RTL1 copy. Excess RTL1, together with absent maternal transcripts, is considered the primary factor behind the phenotype; clinical severity tracks the degree of RTL1 overproduction.

nodes.description: In mice, Rtl1 is expressed in fetal skeletal muscle. Overproduction of Rtl1 after maternal transmission of an Rtl1/Rtl1as deletion causes severe defects of the intercostal, diaphragm and abdominal muscles, with fragile, shrinking fibers and increased centronuclear fibers, and neonatal lethality. These defects are proposed to underlie the bell-shaped thorax, respiratory insufficiency and diastasis recti of KOS.
